method: Separate normally built B19 and B26 Next.js and FastAPI websites with their own complete corpus were served in order at the same private origin. A visitor signed up on B19, saved a profile, saved the professor in Favorites, reopened it and then reopened the same cloud favorite on B26 from the same Chromium browser profile. A private GoTrue/PostgREST/Postgres instance ran the repository migrations. The two current faculty were checked separately on B26. No outreach action was performed.
checks: The B19 favorite POST returned success. Authenticated cloud reads in both browser phases returned the same hashed owner and original ID. The B26 phase created neither an account nor a favorite.

B19 showed the previous regular professor and a draft button. B26 showed the historical status, original personal page, and all three original publication links without a draft button. Its public API carried the sourced adjunct rank.
On B26 Walter remained Associate Professor and Bellamkonda remained Professor. Both personal sources, both draft buttons and all six publication titles remained visible.

The three hosted candidate API responses and Chromium records agreed with the independently assembled 149,954-ID candidate on original ID, named person, campus, profile, rank and quotation, contact state and all nine paper titles.
scope: Private candidate observation. A deployed release of both production services and a successful natural OSU BME directory refresh remain independent.
